pattern: union two differently-headered tables, pivot, compute a difference, rank
question: where did attendance percentage decline the most year on year - average the monthly rates per centre and show the decline in percentage points as a positive figure
gold_sql: WITH combined AS (SELECT "Centre" AS centre, 2023 AS year, "Avg Daily Present" / "Enrolled Kids" * 100.0 AS rate FROM attendance_2023 UNION ALL SELECT centre_name AS centre, 2024 AS year, average_attendance / enrolment * 100.0 AS rate FROM attendance_2024) , by_year AS (SELECT centre, AVG(CASE WHEN year = 2023 THEN rate END) AS avg_2023, AVG(CASE WHEN year = 2024 THEN rate END) AS avg_2024 FROM combined GROUP BY centre) SELECT centre, avg_2023 - avg_2024 AS drop_pp FROM by_year ORDER BY drop_pp DESC, centre LIMIT 1
sql_duckdb: WITH combined AS (SELECT "Centre" AS centre_name, "Month" AS month, "Enrolled Kids" AS enrolment, "Avg Daily Present" AS average_attendance FROM "attendance_2023" UNION ALL SELECT "centre_name", "month", "enrolment", "average_attendance" FROM "attendance_2024"), monthly_rates AS (SELECT centre_name, year, AVG(100.0 * average_attendance / NULLIF(NULLIF(enrolment, 0), 0)) AS avg_rate FROM (SELECT centre_name, month, enrolment, average_attendance, 2023 AS year FROM combined WHERE year = 2023 UNION ALL SELECT centre_name, month, enrolment, average_attendance, 2024 AS year FROM combined WHERE year = 2024) AS sub GROUP BY centre_name, year), pivoted AS (SELECT centre_name, MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2023 THEN avg_rate END) AS rate_2023, MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2024 THEN avg_rate END) AS rate_2024 FROM monthly_rates GROUP BY centre_name) SELECT centre_name, (rate_2023 - rate_2024) AS decline_percentage_points FROM pivoted WHERE NOT rate_2023 IS NULL AND NOT rate_2024 IS NULL ORDER BY decline_percentage_points DESC LIMIT 1

You translate ordinary questions into exactly one read-only DuckDB SELECT or WITH query.

Return SQL only. Never write files, install software, calculate values yourself, or invent columns.

Use only the supplied schema. Preserve relevant scope from earlier turns unless the newest question changes it.

A requested rate must use its stated numerator and denominator. Percentage-point change means later percentage minus earlier percentage, not relative growth.

When the user explicitly asks for percent or percentage, multiply numerator divided by denominator by 100.

When the user asks to compare years or groups without asking for a change, keep those year/group columns and requested measures in the output.

When several known category values are named, filter them separately with IN rather than concatenating them.

Use NULLIF for denominators. Missing values remain missing and are not zero.

Quote column names with double quotes when they contain spaces or odd characters. When two tables describe the same thing with different column names, UNION ALL them with aligned aliases.

For approximate name matching across tables use jaro_winkler_similarity(lower(trim(a)), lower(trim(b))) >= 0.9, keep only the single best match per row (QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY row ORDER BY similarity DESC) = 1), then LEFT JOIN from the reference table so rows with zero matches are kept.

CURRENT QUESTION:
where did attendance percentage decline the most year on year - average the monthly rates per centre and show the decline in percentage points as a positive figure
attempts.response:
WITH combined AS (
  SELECT "Centre" AS centre_name, "Month" AS month, "Enrolled Kids" AS enrolment, "Avg Daily Present" AS average_attendance
  FROM "attendance_2023"
  UNION ALL
  SELECT "centre_name", "month", "enrolment", "average_attendance"
  FROM "attendance_2024"
),
monthly_rates AS (
  SELECT 
    centre_name,
    year,
    AVG(100.0 * average_attendance / NULLIF(enrolment, 0)) AS avg_rate
  FROM (
    SELECT centre_name, month, enrolment, average_attendance, 2023 AS year
    FROM combined
    WHERE year = 2023
    UNION ALL
    SELECT centre_name, month, enrolment, average_attendance, 2024 AS year
    FROM combined
    WHERE year = 2024
  ) sub
  GROUP BY centre_name, year
),
pivoted AS (
  SELECT 
    centre_name,
    MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2023 THEN avg_rate END) AS rate_2023,
    MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2024 THEN avg_rate END) AS rate_2024
  FROM monthly_rates
  GROUP BY centre_name
)
SELECT 
  centre_name,
  (rate_2023 - rate_2024) AS decline_percentage_points
FROM pivoted
WHERE rate_2023 IS NOT NULL AND rate_2024 IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY decline_percentage_points DESC
LIMIT 1;
